proves: THE INVARIANT, stated as an invariant and not as a score: a governed hit resolves from the dictionary under every policy. This token has one long form, so there is nothing for a policy to disagree about, and no policy is permitted to invent a disagreement.
The same invariant on a class-word row. Policies change how a collision is settled and what happens to an unknown; they do not change what an unambiguous catalog row says.

The contrast arm, on fixture data chosen to make the two rules disagree. frequency_baseline ignores the pin and takes the first declared candidate; the governed answer is the pin. This is a comparison on these fixtures and says nothing about any corpus.
Three mechanisms, three answers on this row: the baseline takes Active, the score would take Action off a three-way tie, the pin takes Activity. Only the pin is a decision somebody made.
A most-frequent rule reaches for a gerund here. The penalty table would not, and the pin does not, but the baseline consults neither.
A domain pin against the catalog-wide default. The baseline reproduces the default; the governed answer is what this domain decided.

Line and Loan are the same length and trip no morphology rule, so neither the baseline nor the score can separate them on merit. The pin is the only thing here that is a decision rather than a tie-break.

An unpinned collision. Here the score is right and the baseline reaches for the gerund, which is the direction the disagreement runs on this row - the opposite of ID, and both are in the corpus on purpose.

neural_optin declares an intent this release does not act on: the package carries no statistical tier, so an unknown token is still a passthrough under it. Degrading is better than raising on a documented preset, and governed_hit_is_final means the opt-in could never have changed a known token's answer anyway.

Two of the three tokens are unambiguous and resolve identically under every policy; only the collision moves. A policy can change which candidate wins and it cannot change what an unambiguous row says.
